dataset.name: WANDS's real product.csv (a preregistered 36-key sample) plus automotive's real 17-field native attribute set; end-to-end scoring uses WANDS's real 480 queries and 233,448 real relevance judgments

engine_config.statistics_only: issue42_eval::e2b_statistics_baseline::classify (no access to a field's own name)
engine_config.llm_no_validator: frozen subagent JSON output, first-run-wins per real key restricted to the 2 canonical (unperturbed) configs, evaluation only
engine_config.note: no production commerce_core code was touched by E2b's own implementation, in either correction round

repetitions: 8 independent frozen LLM-proposal artifacts (4 perturbation configurations x 2 runs each); repeated-run agreement (role + physical primitive) measured directly: 107/125 (85.60%), unaffected by either correction round

headline_result.baseline_1_statistics_only: macro F1=0.5366, accepted-structural precision=0.9783 recall=1.0000 (n_accepted=46), abstention_rate=0.0000 -- the honest 'no semantic understanding' floor. Unaffected by either correction round.
headline_result.baseline_2_llm_no_validator: FINAL: macro F1=0.7985, accepted-structural precision=0.9783 recall=1.0000 (n_accepted=46), abstention_rate=0.0000. (Round-1-corrected value was 0.6050 before the round-2 canonical-config fix -- see confirmed_defects_found_and_fixed below.)
headline_result.baseline_3_llm_plus_validator: FINAL: macro F1=0.7697, accepted-structural precision=0.9756 recall=0.8889 (n_accepted=41), abstention_rate=0.0943. (Round-1-corrected value was 0.6269, abstention_rate 0.1321, before round 2.)
headline_result.repeated_run_agreement: 107/125 (85.60%) role+primitive agreement across all 4 configurations -- unaffected by any defect in either correction round. Concrete real disagreement: automotive's thread_size classified enum/bitmap_enum by run 1, numeric/numeric_range by run 2 (now forces Baseline 3 -- never Baseline 2 -- to abstain, per round-2 fix 2).
headline_result.macro_f1_by_configuration: wands_baseline=0.6753 (best, real key visible), wands_noisy=0.6573 (close to baseline -- misleading names did not meaningfully fool the proposing passes), wands_anonymized=0.4900 (clearest real degradation -- losing the key's own name costs real accuracy), automotive=0.2597 (smaller 17-field sample makes each miss proportionally costlier). Unaffected by either correction round (always computed per-config).
headline_result.end_to_end: FINAL: oracle NDCG@10=0.0100 Recall@10=0.0004 (n_queries_scored=270), statistics-only identical to oracle, LLM+validator NDCG@10=0.0100 Recall@10=0.0004 (n_queries_scored=270, was n=251/NDCG=0.0108 before round 2) -- relative NDCG gap vs oracle now 0.00% (was 7.57%). This naive, unranked, substring-matched end-to-end check produces near-floor NDCG for every baseline including oracle and is still flagged unreliable at this magnitude (e2e_check_reliable=false) even at a literal 0% gap -- read as 'no degradation detectable within this coarse check,' not proof of true parity.
headline_result.go_gate: FINAL: zero unsafe accepted (0 found) -- PASS; >=80% recall on retrieval-significant reference features (86.84%, corrected from a vacuous 100.0% -- round-2 fix 3) -- PASS; end-to-end relevance within 5% of oracle (relative gap 0.00%, check itself still flagged unreliable) -- PASS; >=90% repeated-run agreement (85.60%, never a bug) -- FAIL; real structured unseen feed evidence (WANDS) -- PASS.
headline_result.verdict: Still REVISE, not GO, not STOP -- for a cleaner reason than round 1. Four of five gates now pass on an honestly-computed basis; the sole remaining failure (repeated-run agreement) was never part of any of the 5 confirmed defects across both correction rounds and is not a rounding artifact. The corrections materially strengthen the case for the underlying mechanism (macro F1 0.7697 vs the originally-reported 0.6269) without manufacturing a GO verdict -- the gate that still fails, fails on its own real merits. E4/E5/E6 remain explicitly out of scope (protocol/design only) per Issue #42's own scope boundary.

confirmed_defects_found_and_fixed.defect: e2b_ingest::build_catalog matched the real CSV feature key against a descriptor's raw `.key` field, never `.real_key` -- correct for oracle/statistics-only (whose key is always the true feed column) but wrong for the LLM+validator baseline, since WANDS's alphabetically-first config (wands_anonymized) always won the per-real-key first-resolved race, leaving every accepted WANDS field looking for a CSV column (e.g. 'feature_5') that does not exist.
confirmed_defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Added real_key_of(d) -> d.real_key.as_deref().unwrap_or(&d.key) and used it everywhere build_catalog keys its typed_keys/typed_by_key maps.
confirmed_defects_found_and_fixed.post_correction_value: LLM + validator: NDCG@10=0.0108 Recall@10=0.0004 (n_queries_scored=251), directly comparable to oracle's own NDCG@10=0.0100 (n_queries_scored=270)

confirmed_defects_found_and_fixed.found_by: a fresh, independent adversarial-review subagent with no implementation task, per Issue #42's own governance
confirmed_defects_found_and_fixed.defect: per_config_runs is a BTreeMap<String, Vec<LlmPassOutput>>, iterated in alphabetical config-name order (automotive, wands_anonymized, wands_baseline, wands_noisy), not the intended 'unperturbed configs first' order. no_validator_by_key/validated_by_key used .entry().or_insert_with() across ALL 4 configs, so every one of WANDS's 36 real keys silently drew its headline classification from wands_anonymized (alphabetically first among the 3 WANDS configs) rather than wands_baseline.

confirmed_defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Added CANONICAL_CONFIGS=[wands_baseline, automotive] and restricted no_validator_by_key/validated_by_key to only draw from those two unperturbed configs. per_config_f1 (degradation analysis) and stability_agreements (run1-vs-run2 within one config) were both already correct and untouched. confirmed_defects_found_and_fixed.defect: The preregistered 'type consistency' validator check (ISSUE42_PROTOCOL.md's E2b validator spec, verbatim: no key may be accepted as both Enum/Boolean and Numeric across different perturbation runs without at least one being flagged abstain) was never implemented anywhere. validate()'s single-descriptor signature has no visibility into another run's proposal for the same key. The concrete case this experiment's own data already contained -- automotive's real thread_size run1=enum/run2=numeric disagreement -- sailed through fully accepted with no abstain.
confirmed_defects_found_and_fixed.pre_correction_value: thread_size accepted as structural in Baseline 3 with no abstain despite the unresolved run1/run2 type conflict
confirmed_defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Added e2b_validator::cross_run_type_conflict(a, b) -> bool (false whenever either side abstains), wired into build_baselines_2_and_3: a canonical config's own run1-vs-run2 conflict forces that key's Baseline 3 entry to abstain. Baseline 2 (explicitly 'no validator') is deliberately untouched by this check.
confirmed_defects_found_and_fixed.post_correction_value: thread_size forced to abstain in Baseline 3; Baseline 2 unaffected

confirmed_defects_found_and_fixed.fix: Applied the identical !abstain && is_structural(semantic_role) filter used by print_and_score.

note: All five defects across both correction rounds were found before being trusted (Issue #42's own 'do not trust the experiment author' governance, applied recursively to the fresh reviewer's own findings too -- each was independently re-verified against the actual source before being accepted), were entirely within the evaluation harness (crates/issue42-eval), and involved zero changes to commerce_core or to any preregistered GO-gate threshold. All pre- and post-correction numbers, across both rounds, are preserved in docs/research/artifacts/i42_e2b_run1/ per rule 9 (never silently replace an invalidated number): main_run1_pre_correction_buggy.txt/summary_pre_correction_buggy.json (before round 1), main_run1_round3_pre_final_review.txt/summary_round3_pre_final_review.json (after round 1, before round 2), main_run1.txt/summary.json (final, after both rounds).
